assertion.statement: The zero vertex of every linear-orbit (d+1)-cube is a continuous function of its other vertices on one fixed compact set.
assertion.objects: Fixed d-step nilmanifold M, compact Sigma inside M^(2^(d+1)-1), continuous map P and all linear-orbit cubes.
assertion.hypotheses: A fixed nilmanifold of step at most d; in this application the group is connected simply connected with a cocompact lattice.
assertion.quantifiers: Every g,x and all integers n,h, with no bound on orbit parameters.
assertion.parameter_range: Every fixed d>=1; actual application has d=s-2.
assertion.uniformity: Sigma and P depend only on the fixed nilmanifold, not N,g,x.
assertion.constants: No quantitative modulus is assumed; compactness supplies finite approximation data after epsilon is fixed.
assertion.normalizations: Right lattice quotient and the exact nonzero-vertex cube map; no polynomial orbit is substituted until it is linearized.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Step smaller than d is allowed. No assertion is made for a non-nilpotent or changing geometry.
assertion.limit_order: Fix M and the cube constraint before selecting the test, orbit, averaging scale or N.

supplier.locator: Proposition11.5 and Definition11.4 p1799; published AppendixE proof is retained as a source premise

assertion.statement: The composed test F(P(z)) has a finite tensor approximation with uniform bounds over the fixed bounded Lipschitz test class.
assertion.objects: Coordinate Lipschitz functions on compact Sigma, complex coefficients c_a, one-bounded factors H_(omega,a), finite uniform test net.
assertion.hypotheses: Published continuous cube constraint, fixed compact M, fixed norm and Lipschitz bounds, positive epsilon.
assertion.quantifiers: Every test in the fixed class and every cube point z in Sigma.
assertion.parameter_range: Any fixed d,M,L and epsilon; finite tensor dimension 2^(d+1)-1.
assertion.uniformity: The finite coefficient sum, number of terms and factor bounds are uniform in F,g,x,N.
assertion.constants: Keep sum |c_a|; allocate epsilon/2 to the net and epsilon/2 to approximation.
assertion.normalizations: Complex Stone-Weierstrass algebra contains constants, separates points and is closed under conjugation.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Factors are scaled to the unit disk with their magnitudes absorbed into coefficients; they are not silently normalized without compensation.
assertion.limit_order: Choose the finite net and tensor data before the orbit and averaging parameters.

supplier.locator: Stone-Weierstrass and Arzela-Ascoli argument in proof11.2 pp1799-1801, applied explicitly in localSection2

assertion.statement: Probability averaging over all integer shifts preserves the uniform cube approximation error and gives a sampled cutoff with uniformly bounded Fourier l1 norm.
assertion.objects: Fixed smooth sigma, S_N=sum sigma(h/N), probability mu_N, centered cyclic sample w_N and its Fourier coefficients.
assertion.hypotheses: sigma supported[-1,2], equal1 on[0,1], values in[0,1]; Q=C_d N with fixed sufficiently large C_d.
assertion.quantifiers: Every N>=1 and every cyclic frequency, including zero.
assertion.parameter_range: Fixed d>=1; C_d also larger than2^(d+1) when interval normalization is used.
assertion.uniformity: Fourier l1 bound independent of N, from O(1/r_star^2) decay.
assertion.constants: N<=S_N<=4N; keep all S_N powers and second-derivative constants.
assertion.normalizations: Start with an all-integer probability average, not a hard [N] average widened later.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Smooth zero extension handles support boundaries; small N satisfies the same estimates.
assertion.limit_order: Fix sigma and C_d, normalize the integer average, then transfer its exact sum to the cyclic group.

supplier.locator: Local normalized smoothing and discrete second-difference proof

assertion.statement: Each Fourier term of the weighted cube average is bounded by the cyclic U^(d+1) norm of the distinguished input.
assertion.objects: Zero-extended v, bounded nonzero-vertex functions, Fourier phases in h and the full cyclic cube.
assertion.hypotheses: d+1>=2; all nonzero-vertex factors bounded by1; exact cyclic representation with no wrapped conflicting arguments.
assertion.quantifiers: Every Fourier frequency tuple, every bounded factor collection and every complex v.
assertion.parameter_range: Q=C_d N with C_d>10(d+2) and sufficiently large for interval normalization.
assertion.uniformity: Bounds depend only on d and the fixed cutoff; no orbit dependence.
assertion.constants: Track (Q/N)(Q/S_N)^(d+1), Fourier l1 product and the finite tensor coefficient sum.
assertion.normalizations: Absorb each h_j phase using vertices e_j+e_k and e_k, k!=j; the distinguished input is unchanged.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Complex conjugations are placed in vertex functions to match(B.12); d=1 still has two coordinate directions.
assertion.limit_order: Transfer exact sums, expand cutoffs, apply Gowers-CS termwise, then compare cyclic and normalized interval norms.

assertion.statement: A fixed degree-d polynomial nilsequence can be used in this linear converse on fixed geometry of step at most d.
assertion.objects: Exact same-step linear model, boundedly normalized test, finite family and fixed metric comparison.
assertion.hypotheses: Rational connected polynomial model with cocompact lattice and a fixed bounded Lipschitz test.
assertion.quantifiers: All polynomial coefficients, all interval lengths and every member of the fixed finite family.
assertion.parameter_range: d=s-2>=1 in the assembly; no increase of step is allowed.
assertion.uniformity: Geometry and Lipschitz multiplier independent of N and coefficients; take a finite maximum.
assertion.constants: Sequence and correlation unchanged; retain the fixed Lipschitz multiplier and any initial norm normalization.
assertion.normalizations: Use the accepted right-increment P1 construction, not the defective full-P0 suspension.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Trivial and constant models covered by the accepted unit; old universal unnormalized projection clause is not claimed.
assertion.limit_order: Linearize exactly first, then apply the proved converse with error chosen from the positive correlation.
